A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same RS-vHeat study, with complete readable main text, Figures 1–8, Tables 1–10, equations, and Appendices A–D. Content can be reliably matched despite pagination differences.

before.justification: v2 reports original benchmark evaluations, efficiency measurements, and ablations in Section 4, plus qualitative predictions and per-category detection results in Appendix D.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experimental results, including the benchmark tables, ablations, efficiency plots, and supplementary results in Appendix D.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same frequency masking, heat conduction operator, frequency value and spatial correction embeddings, reconstruction decoders, and combined loss. No algorithm or architecture changes are documented.

E1.justification: Both retain the same optical/SAR pretraining data and ten downstream datasets spanning segmentation, object detection, classification, and change detection. Section 4 and Appendix D introduce no different coverage.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is identical within each corresponding experiment in Tables 1–8 and 10. Figures 7–8 also retain the same qualitative comparison methods.

E3.justification: Training budgets, input sizes, splits, task heads, and evaluation metrics in Section 4 and Appendix D are unchanged. Figure 4 retains the single-A100, batch-size-32 efficiency protocol.

E4.justification: The masking/SCE learning curves in Figure 5, loss-component ablations in Table 9, and qualitative analyses in Figures 7–8 are retained without changes to the questions tested or evidence.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or error bars. No uncertainty-reporting practice is added or revised.

E6.justification: All corresponding numerical entries, plotted results, and qualitative predictions are unchanged. Examples include DIOR mAP50 of 82.30 in Table 4, FAIR1M-2.0 mAP of 48.29 in Table 7, and LEVIR-CD F1 of 93.48 in Table 8.

T1.justification: Equations 1–20 are retained, including the heat-equation derivation in Appendix B and DCT/IDCT masking formulations in Appendix C. Mathematical assumptions and reasoning are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same scientific claims, including multimodal heat-conduction modeling, evaluation across four tasks and ten datasets, and the stated memory, FLOPs, and throughput advantages.

C2.justification: The thermal-space interpretation, explanations of masking and loss-component benefits, and accuracy–efficiency tradeoffs remain unchanged. No substantive limitation or applicability qualification is added or removed.

D1.justification: Section 4.1 and Appendices C–D retain the same architecture configuration, hardware, hyperparameters, preprocessing, and downstream implementation details. Both abstracts still state that code will be made publicly available.

R1.justification: The cited works, reference list, and positioning relative to vHeat and other remote-sensing models are unchanged, including Section 2 and Appendix A.

P1.justification: v3 revises author-affiliation superscripts, reduces the affiliation list from eight entries to five, and adds the laboratory acronym TCAT. Scientific prose, headings, and section order remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The shorter affiliation block reflows the main text and float placement. Table 7 moves from page 9 to page 8, and Table 9 moves above Figure 5 on page 9. Figure and table contents, captions, and structures are retained.

improvement.justification: v3 updates affiliations and makes limited pagination and table-placement adjustments while preserving the complete scientific argument, experimental evidence, derivations, and reproducibility information. These presentation changes do not materially improve or diminish overall readability or scientific quality.
